trivia.fact: Tom Cruise performed his own stunts for the Shanghai rooftop chase scene, one of the most iconic running sequences in cinema.
Director J.J. Abrams commented "I loved watching you run" during filming of the #1 ranked running scene.
The famous running scene took 6-7 takes to get perfect, with a Spidercam rig built specifically for the scene.

formBreakdown.overallAnalysis: Peak Tom Cruise running form. Elbows sharp, eyes forward, feet a blur. This film showcases the fastest Cruise has ever looked on screen.

runningAnalysis.speedAnalysis: Clocked at running 15.3 mph (24.6 km/h) during the famous running sequence at age 43.
runningAnalysis.comparisonToAthletes: Running at speeds comparable to Olympic sprinters during action sequences.

trivia.fact: The famous chair throw scene where Cruise wipes out was unplanned. Director Michael Mann kept it in the final cut for authenticity.
Ranked #2 overall for the window crash scene - one of the most realistic-looking stunts in the franchise.
Times Square was closed for 3 hours on a Sunday morning in November for the iconic empty running scene.
The empty Times Square scene symbolizes the character's fear of being alone, manifesting in his dreams.
First film to fully showcase Tom Cruise's soon-to-be-famous running form (elbows and knees).

formBreakdown.overallAnalysis: The film where the iconic Tom Cruise running style was first on full display.

trivia.fact: The 7-second cigarette-smoking running scene in sunglasses is described as "when Cruise became Tom Cruise".
Tom Cruise broke his ankle during the rooftop running scene but continued filming. He said "I loved doing this, but it hurt."
The broken ankle happened at the very end of the famous rooftop jump scene. The moment is visible in the final film.
